title: Atlanta kicks off World Cup with community pep rally
text:
ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens was on hand Tuesday for a community pep rally on the city’s westside ahead of the FIFA World Cup.

>> WATCH THE PRESS CONFERENCE AHEAD OF THE PEP RALLY:

Hundreds of kids packed the event at the CT Martin Recreation Center getting their faces painted, playing soccer, and getting “passports” stamped as Atlanta puts the finishing touches on plans to welcome what leaders expect will be hundreds of thousands of visitors during the tournament.

“It’s officially here y’all,” said Dickens. “The first match is six days away.”

Dickens said Tuesday marks four years since FIFA announced Atlanta as a host city.

“We’ve trained more than 400 city employees to help welcome our visitors from around the world to ensure that Atlanta is ready to be a host to an international audience,” Dickens said.

The mayor said preparation has included years of planning meetings and public safety drills, along with infrastructure upgrades.

He said they’ve resurfaced 12 miles of streets, restriped 200 intersections, installed 150 new streetlights and repaired 14 miles of sidewalks.

Dickens also highlighted efforts to engage kids and neighborhoods through soccer-related programming with Soccer in the Streets.

As the first match approaches, Lamar Stewart with Showcase Atlanta said fans can expect special surprises at businesses and community centers across the city.

“We will be having some fun activations happening around town,” Stewart said. “We will also be providing some tickets to the games and to our citizens.”

Dickens and Atlanta City Councilmember Andrea Boone said the city’s goal extends beyond the World Cup itself towards the legacy it leaves behind.

“It’s an opportunity for a young person in Atlanta to see new possibilities,” Dickens said. “It’s an opportunity for a small business to reach new customers.”

“The greatest legacy of an event like this is not only what happens on the global stage, but what it leaves behind in our neighborhood,” said Boone.

Organizers with Showcase Atlanta also announced a city-wide scavenger hunt throughout the tournament, along with a free concert featuring Ludacris in Piedmont Park.

The first World Cup match in Atlanta takes place on June 15 at noon with Cape Verde vs. Spain.
